sections.h2: Where is Grady County, Oklahoma, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Grady County lies in south-central Oklahoma and covers 1,105.30 square miles, with Chickasha as the county seat. The Oklahoma Historical Society places Canadian County to the north, McClain and Garvin to the east, Stephens to the south, and Caddo and Comanche to the west.

The Canadian River forms the northern border and the Washita River runs through the middle of the county. Most of the land is rolling prairie, with sandstone hills in the west and southwest. Those rivers and their creeks drain the county, which is why farm and pasture acreage has always been a big part of Grady County tax rolls.

Eleven towns besides Chickasha were incorporated at the time of the 2010 census: Alex, Amber, Bradley, Bridge Creek, Minco, Ninnekah, Norge, Pocasset, Rush Springs, Tuttle and Verden. The same treasurer bills homes in all of them.

sections.h2: What does the Grady County census snapshot say about housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau counts about 55,868 people and 23,332 housing units in Grady County for 2019 to 2023. Those numbers describe the kind of housing a seller is dealing with.

MeasureGrady County
Population55,868
Housing units23,332
Median home value$187,900
Median household income$75,730
Owner-occupied share75%
Median year built1981

Three out of four occupied homes are owned, and the typical house is more than four decades old. Older roofs, wiring and plumbing are the usual items that turn up during a buyer's inspection. The county's 2020 census population was 54,800, up from 45,516 in 2000.

sections.h2: What drives the Grady County economy?
sections.html:
Agriculture, dairy, oil and gas, and manufacturing in Chickasha have each had a turn as the main driver. In 2000 ranchers ran an estimated 110,000 head of cattle, and wheat covered 105,000 acres, dominating crop production.

Bill Braum located his main dairy in the county in 1975 with a herd of ten thousand Holsteins and added a processing plant and distribution center in 1987. The Tuttle entry calls Braum's Dairy, between Tuttle and Minco, a major area employer. Oil and gas drilling began near the Grady and Stephens county line in the late 1910s, and the county produced about 3.8 million barrels of crude and more than 104 million thousand cubic feet of gas in 2000.

  • Chickasha has long been the shipping point for cattle and cotton.
  • The University of Science and Arts of Oklahoma is in Chickasha.
  • The county had fourteen companies with over one hundred employees in 2000.

Northeastern Grady County, around Tuttle and Bridge Creek, has taken on commuters who work in the Oklahoma City area, per the state encyclopedia. Tuttle sits about twenty-seven miles southwest of Oklahoma City at the junction of State Highways 37 and 92.

Interstate 44, also called the H. E. Bailey Turnpike, runs through Grady County from northeast to southwest. U.S. Highways 62, 81 and 277 also cross it, along with a long list of state highways.

TypeRoutes named by the state encyclopedia
InterstateI-44 (H. E. Bailey Turnpike)

Good highway access is a selling point for homes in the north end of the county, where drive times to Oklahoma City are shorter. Homes in the southwest hills sit further from the interstate.

sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax in Grady County?
sections.html:
The Grady County Treasurer sends and collects the bill, and the County Assessor sets the value. The treasurer's office is at 326 W Choctaw in Chickasha, phone 405-224-5337, and it is open Monday to Friday from 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM.

Payment options listed by the office include in person, by mail, by phone with a card, in the courthouse drop box and online through the tax roll inquiry. Online fees are $1.50 for an e-check, $3.95 for a debit card and 2.95% of the total for a credit card. The office asks owners who have not received a statement by the end of November to call and check what is owed.

Oklahoma bills combine county, city or town, and school district levies, so two houses in the same county can have different totals.

sections.h2: When is Grady County property tax due, and what happens if it is late?
sections.html:
Under 68 O.S. 2913, an owner who pays half or more before January 1 has until before April 1 for the balance. Anyone who pays less than half by then sees the entire levy become delinquent on January 1.

The Grady County treasurer states that a postmark counts when you are meeting a deadline, except for the publication notice and the June resale. Late balances add a penalty of 1.5% per month, charged on the 16th, plus fees if the account has been published. A statement marked BT, for back tax, needs a phone call for the true total.

  • Unpaid statements do not pause the clock.
  • Publication adds fees.
  • A June resale is the county's sale of delinquent property.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Grady County valuation?
sections.html:
Start with a written informal protest to the county assessor within 30 calendar days of the date the valuation notice was mailed. The Oklahoma Tax Commission's Form 974 describes this step under 68 O.S. 2876.

  1. Fill out Form 974 and state the value you think is right, with sales, comparables or an appraisal.
  2. If you bought the property in the last two years, give the purchase date and price on the form.
  3. Join the hearing in person or by phone.
  4. Expect the assessor's written decision within seven calendar days.
  5. Appeal to the county board of equalization on Form 976 within 15 calendar days of the mailed decision.

A parcel with no change in value from the prior year can be protested until the first Monday in April. Proceedings should be done by May 31 or the board's adjournment date. If you skip the 30-day window, the assessor's value stands for that year.

sections.h2: What should a Grady County seller check before closing?
sections.html:
Ask the treasurer for a written balance, because the total may include back taxes, penalties or published fees. Then confirm there are no other claims against the parcel.

Deeds are recorded by the Grady County Clerk, which charges $18 for the first page and $2 for each additional page. Documentary stamp tax is $1.50 per thousand dollars of consideration, which equals the $0.75 per $500 in 68 O.S. 3201 and applies when the price is over $100. The clerk's FAQ says land records are computerized from 1929 to the present and that documents delivered by 4 pm are filed the same day.

Our companion page on the Grady County Clerk walks through recording in more detail.

sections.h2: What do Grady County sellers usually face?
sections.html:
Most sellers here have a house that is older than the median 1981 build year or a rural parcel with acreage. Some inherited the property, and others live outside Oklahoma and cannot easily manage repairs.

  • Roof and system updates a buyer will ask about.
  • Pasture or crop land that is taxed differently from a town lot.
  • Unpaid taxes with a monthly penalty running.
  • Distance from Chickasha services in smaller towns such as Verden, Norge or Ninnekah.

Pulling the treasurer's balance and your deed before you talk to any buyer keeps the process quick.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Grady County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay at the Grady County Treasurer, 326 W Choctaw in Chickasha, by mail, by phone with a card, in the drop box at the courthouse, or online through the tax roll inquiry. The phone number is 405-224-5337.

faqs.q: How much is the late penalty in Grady County?
faqs.a: The treasurer states a penalty of 1.5% per month, charged on the 16th of each month, plus fees if the account has been published. A statement marked BT needs a call for the total.

faqs.q: How long do I have to protest my Grady County value?
faqs.a: You have 30 calendar days from the date the valuation notice was mailed to file a written protest with the assessor. The appeal to the board of equalization must follow within 15 calendar days of the assessor's mailed decision.

faqs.q: Is a Grady County house worth less because of its age?
faqs.a: The median home here was built in 1981, so age alone does not set value. An older roof or system will matter to buyers, and a Form 974 protest should use sales, comparables or an appraisal.
